system_description.narrative_title: AI boom meets political recoil amid energy and security shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated AI and data‑center investment wave has collided with a political backlash—most visibly after a Democratic midterm sweep—sparking a sharp market correction, credit stress in AI infrastructure and a nascent policy drive to slow the buildout. Simultaneously, renewed Middle East tensions and Russia‑Ukraine strikes are driving volatile oil swings and risk premia, forcing markets and central banks to reprice growth and rates. China's selective tech controls and industrial adjustments add supply‑chain friction, making the whole open system highly sensitive to policy, financing and conflict shocks.
system_description.scope: Cross‑border interactions among major‑power foreign policies, global capital markets, AI/tech firms and the data‑centre financing chain, energy producers and markets, regional conflicts (Middle East, Ukraine), and the regulatory and monetary institutions that mediate them.
system_description.super_system: The international political‑economic order (the integrated system of sovereign states, global markets, and transnational corporations).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and credit plumbing
U.S. domestic politics and technology/regulatory policy
Middle East security and global energy supply
China's tech‑industrial and trade policy complex

variables.name: AI investment boom and backlash
variables.description: Big tech firms, investors and democratically elected governments are recalibrating AI infrastructure spending and regulation as financial strains, local pushback against data‑centres and political scrutiny dent the business model powering the AI buildout.

variables.name: US–Iran regional escalation risk
variables.description: The United States, Iran and regional proxies — with active mediation by Gulf states — are engaged in a tense cycle of strikes, diplomatic exchanges and contingency planning that raises the probability of wider military escalation and shifts regional security dynamics.

variables.name: Russian war in Ukraine and infrastructure strikes
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed by Western security assistance and diplomatic efforts, are locked in a protracted war marked by evolving battlefield dynamics and repeated strikes on critical infrastructure that are reshaping European security planning.

variables.name: China–West high‑tech competition
variables.description: China and Western/Asian technology powers are intensifying an economic and strategic rivalry through export controls, investment screening and state industrial policy aimed at securing chip, robotics and AI supply chains and promoting technological self‑reliance.

variables.name: Global financial re‑pricing and volatility
variables.description: Global investors, central banks and bond markets are rapidly repricing risk across equities, credit and rates in response to election outcomes, strong macro data and geopolitical shocks, altering capital flows and funding conditions worldwide.
